syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploration
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

chapters.title: Exploration: Entering the World of Secondary Science

topics.title: Models: simplifying complex systems

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a scientific model is a simplified representation of a real system that keeps only what matters for a given question.
Decide which details to keep and which to ignore when building a simple model for a stated question.

topics.title: The language of science: terms, symbols, units and mathematics

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that scientific words and symbols have precise, agreed meanings that allow clear communication.
Explain why agreed international (SI) units are needed for comparing results and avoiding errors.
Describe an equation as a compact statement of how quantities are related, used after understanding the situation.

topics.title: Laws, theories and principles

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between a scientific law, a theory and a principle using examples.
Explain that a scientific theory is a tested, evidence-based explanation that stays open to revision.

topics.title: Predictions, their limits and checking claims

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how well-established laws, theories and models are used to make testable predictions.
Evaluate claims using evidence and explain why failed predictions strengthen science.

topics.title: Estimation and approximate reasoning

concepts.learning_objective: Make a rough estimate by identifying the relevant quantities and multiplying reasonable values.
Use estimates to judge whether an answer is reasonable or impossible.

topics.title: Connected branches of science and science as a human activity

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how several branches of science and mathematics combine to solve a real problem.
Describe science as a human, collaborative and self-correcting way of understanding the world.

chapters.title: Cell: The Building Block of Life

topics.title: How to Study Cells

concepts.learning_objective: State the limit of resolution of the human eye and why microscopes are needed to study cells.
Calculate total magnification and compare light and electron microscopes.
Estimate the real size of a cell from the field of view of a microscope.

topics.title: Cell Membrane: The Universal Feature of a Cell

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the cell membrane is selectively permeable.
Distinguish diffusion from osmosis and explain osmosis in cells.
Predict the effect of isotonic, hypotonic and hypertonic solutions on a cell.
Describe the composition and fluid-mosaic structure of the cell membrane.

topics.title: Cell Wall: The Outer Covering of Cells

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the composition, permeability and functions of the cell wall.
Compare how plant and animal cells respond to a concentrated solution.

topics.title: The Cell Interior: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells by nucleus, organelles and size.
Describe the cytoskeleton and cell inclusions in the cytoplasm.

topics.title: Nucleus, Ribosomes, ER, Golgi Apparatus and Lysosomes

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the nucleus, chromatin, chromosomes, DNA and genes.
Explain the roles of ribosomes and of rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Describe how the Golgi apparatus packages materials and lysosomes clean up the cell.

topics.title: Mitochondria, Plastids and Vacuoles

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of mitochondria and their role in releasing energy as ATP.
Distinguish chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts by pigment and function.
Explain how the central vacuole stores materials and keeps plant cells firm.

topics.title: How Cells Grow and Divide: Mitosis and Meiosis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that mitosis forms two genetically identical cells for growth and repair.
Explain that meiosis forms four gametes with half the chromosome number.
Interpret the observation of dividing cells in an onion root tip.

topics.title: Cell Theory and the Life Span of Cells

concepts.learning_objective: State the classical cell theory and the scientists who formulated it.
Explain contact inhibition and how its loss leads to tumours.
Explain the role of programmed cell death in development.

topics.title: Tissues, division of labour and why plant and animal tissues differ

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the hierarchy cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism and the division of labour it brings.
Explain how a fixed, upright life and photosynthesis make plant tissues differ from animal tissues.

topics.title: Meristematic tissues: apical, lateral and intercalary

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the location and role of apical, lateral and intercalary meristems.
Relate the features of meristematic cells to continuous cell division.
Explain how meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and differentiate into permanent tissue.

topics.title: Permanent tissues: epidermis and simple permanent tissues

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the epidermis, cuticle, root hairs and stomata and their protective roles.
Distinguish parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma by cell walls, living state and function.

topics.title: Complex permanent tissues and plant tissue systems

concepts.learning_objective: Name the components of xylem and phloem and state what each transports.
Classify plant tissues into the dermal, ground and vascular tissue systems.

topics.title: Epithelial and connective tissues

concepts.learning_objective: Match types of epithelium to their structure, function and location in the body.
Describe blood as a fluid connective tissue and the roles of its components.
Distinguish bone, cartilage, tendons and ligaments by matrix and function.

topics.title: Muscular and nervous tissues

concepts.learning_objective: Compare skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle by structure, location and control.
Identify the cell body, dendrites, axon and axon terminals of a neuron and their roles.

topics.title: Musculoskeletal system, joints and skeletal system

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how muscles, tendons, bones and joints work together under nervous control to produce movement.
Identify ball and socket, hinge, pivot and fixed joints and the movements they allow.
Describe how the vertebral column and rib cage protect organs yet allow movement.

topics.title: Totipotency and plant tissue culture
topics.ncert_sections: Think as a Scientist; Bridging Science and Society

concepts.learning_objective: Explain totipotency through dedifferentiation and redifferentiation in Steward's carrot experiment.
Evaluate applications of plant tissue culture and of Agrobacterium in improving crops.

topics.title: Position, distance travelled and displacement

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the position of an object using a reference point, distance and direction, and decide whether it is at rest or in motion.
Distinguish between total distance travelled and displacement for motion in a straight line.

topics.title: Average speed and average velocity

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate average speed as total distance travelled divided by the time interval.
Calculate average velocity as displacement divided by the time interval and state its direction.
Distinguish between uniform and non-uniform motion in a straight line.

topics.title: Average acceleration

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate average acceleration as the change in velocity divided by the time interval.
Relate the direction of acceleration to whether the magnitude of velocity is increasing or decreasing.
Recognise that an object falling freely has a constant acceleration of about 9.8 m/s squared.

topics.title: Plotting and interpreting position-time graphs

concepts.learning_objective: Plot a position-time graph from a data table by choosing axes and suitable scales.
Interpret the shape of a position-time graph to identify rest, constant velocity or changing velocity.
Calculate the magnitude of velocity from the slope of a straight-line position-time graph.

topics.title: Velocity-time graphs

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the slope of a velocity-time graph as acceleration and calculate it.
Calculate displacement from the area enclosed by a velocity-time graph and the time axis.

topics.title: Kinematic equations for constant acceleration

concepts.learning_objective: State the kinematic equations v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at squared and v squared = u squared + 2as and the condition for their use.
Apply the kinematic equations to find velocity, displacement, acceleration or time.
Explain how the stopping distance of a vehicle depends on its initial velocity and braking.

topics.title: Motion in a plane and uniform circular motion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify examples of motion in two dimensions.
Explain why uniform circular motion is accelerated even though the speed is constant.
Calculate distance, displacement and average speed for motion along a circle.

topics.title: Classifying mixtures: homogeneous and heterogeneous

concepts.learning_objective: Identify homogeneous mixtures (solutions) by their uniform composition.
Recognise heterogeneous mixtures, including those with a gas as one component.

topics.title: Solutions and their concentration

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what the concentration of a solution means and why the right proportion matters.
Calculate concentration as % m/m, % m/v and % v/v and choose the suitable form.

topics.title: Solubility and solubility curves

concepts.learning_objective: Define solubility and a saturated solution at a given temperature.
Interpret solubility data and curves to predict the effect of temperature.

topics.title: Crystallization

concepts.learning_objective: Explain crystallization as separation based on change of solubility with temperature.
Relate the rate of cooling to the size and shape of crystals formed.

topics.title: Distillation and paper chromatography

concepts.learning_objective: Use boiling point differences to decide when simple or fractional distillation applies.
Explain how paper chromatography separates the components of a coloured mixture.

topics.title: Immiscible liquids, sublimation and alloys

concepts.learning_objective: Separate two immiscible liquids using a separating funnel based on density.
Separate a sublimable solid from a non-sublimable one by sublimation.
Describe alloys as homogeneous mixtures whose components cannot be separated physically.

topics.title: Suspensions, centrifugation and coagulation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the properties of suspensions.
Explain how centrifugation separates heavier particles from a liquid.
Explain how a coagulant such as alum clears muddy water.

topics.title: Colloids and the Tyndall effect

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish colloids from solutions and suspensions by particle size and behaviour.
Explain the Tyndall effect and identify mixtures that show it.

topics.title: The Concept of Force

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise force as a quantity that needs both magnitude and direction, measured in newtons (N).
Explain how a spring balance measures the magnitude of a force and the range of forces we meet.

topics.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish balanced from unbalanced forces and predict whether an object will move.
Calculate the magnitude and direction of the net force when forces act along the same line.

topics.title: The Force of Friction

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how friction acts opposite to motion and brings moving objects to rest.
Relate the distance travelled and spring balance readings to the friction offered by different surfaces.
Identify the normal force and weight acting on an object on a surface and how they balance.

topics.title: Newton's First Law of Motion

concepts.learning_objective: State Newton's first law and apply it to objects with zero net force.
Explain inertia and Galileo's argument that no force is needed to maintain uniform motion.
Interpret position-time and velocity-time graphs of objects with no net force.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion

concepts.learning_objective: Apply F = ma to find force, acceleration or displacement of an object.
Define one newton and calculate weight using F = mg.
Explain why increasing the stopping time reduces the force, as in catching a ball or airbags.

topics.title: Newton's Third Law of Motion

concepts.learning_objective: State Newton's third law and explain that the paired forces act on different objects.
Explain walking, rowing and recoil using Newton's third law.
Explain rocket lift-off and slowing down in space using Newton's third law.

topics.title: Forces Acting on a System of Objects

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish internal forces from external forces for a system of connected objects.
Calculate the acceleration of connected objects treated as a single system.

topics.title: Work done by a constant force

concepts.learning_objective: Define work done by a constant force and express its SI unit, the joule.
Identify situations in which the work done by a force is zero.
Distinguish between positive and negative work from the directions of force and displacement.

topics.title: Work-energy theorem and forms of energy

concepts.learning_objective: State the work-energy theorem and relate work done on an object to its change in energy.
Recognise that energy is transferred by mechanical work and also by heat, radiation, sound and electric circuits.
Identify different forms of energy and their conversion from one form to another.

topics.title: Kinetic energy

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and use the expression K = (1/2)mv^2 for kinetic energy.
Analyse how kinetic energy depends on mass and velocity and apply it to stopping problems.

topics.title: Potential energy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain potential energy as energy stored by deformation or by the relative positions of interacting objects.
Calculate gravitational potential energy using U = mgh near the Earth's surface.

topics.title: Conservation of mechanical energy

concepts.learning_objective: State that the sum of kinetic and potential energy stays constant when only gravity does work.
Describe the interchange of kinetic and potential energy in a swinging pendulum.
Use energy conservation and the work-energy theorem to find speeds, heights and losses.

topics.title: Power

concepts.learning_objective: Define power as the rate of doing work and state its units.
Calculate average power from work done or energy change and time taken.

topics.title: Simple machines: pulley and inclined plane

concepts.learning_objective: Define effort, load and mechanical advantage of a simple machine.
Explain how a fixed pulley provides convenience by changing the direction of effort.
Calculate the mechanical advantage L/h of an inclined plane and the effort it requires.

topics.title: Lever

concepts.learning_objective: Apply effort x effort arm = load x load arm to balance and mechanical advantage problems.
Classify levers into three classes by the relative positions of fulcrum, load and effort.

topics.title: Roots of atomic theory and Thomson's model

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the ideas of Kanada, Democritus and Dalton about indivisible particles of matter.
Explain how the study of cathode rays led to the discovery of the electron.
Describe Thomson's plum pudding model of a neutral atom.

topics.title: Gold foil experiment and Rutherford's nuclear model

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the observations of the alpha particle scattering experiment.
State the features of Rutherford's nuclear model and the relative sizes of atom and nucleus.
Describe the charge and mass of the proton and why atoms are electrically neutral.

topics.title: Limitations of Rutherford's model and Bohr's model

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Rutherford's model could not account for the stability of atoms.
State Bohr's postulates of stationary states, shells and energy levels.

topics.title: Discovery of the neutron and symbols of elements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the neutron accounts for atomic mass and helps hold the nucleus together.
Apply IUPAC norms to write and interpret symbols of elements.

topics.title: Atomic number and mass number

concepts.learning_objective: Define atomic number and relate it to the identity of an element.
Calculate mass number and the number of neutrons from nucleon counts.
Interpret the standard notation showing symbol, atomic number and mass number.

topics.title: Distribution of electrons in energy levels

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the Bohr-Bury rules, including the 2n squared rule, to the filling of shells.
Write the electronic configuration of the first eighteen elements.

topics.title: Valency: combining capacity of an atom

concepts.learning_objective: Relate valence electrons and a complete octet to the reactivity of an atom.
Determine the valency of an element from its electronic configuration or formula.

topics.title: Isotopes, average atomic mass and isobars

concepts.learning_objective: Define isotopes and explain why they have similar chemical properties.
Calculate the weighted average atomic mass of an element from isotopic abundances.
Identify isobars and distinguish them from isotopes.

topics.title: Law of Conservation of Mass

concepts.learning_objective: State the Law of Conservation of Mass and verify it from given masses of reactants and products.
Explain why a reaction that releases a gas must be done in a closed system to show that mass is conserved.

topics.title: Law of Constant Proportions

concepts.learning_objective: State the Law of Constant (Definite) Proportions and use a fixed mass ratio to find unknown masses.
Explain why the law applies to compounds and not to mixtures.

topics.title: Dalton's Atomic Theory

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the postulates of Dalton's Atomic Theory.
Use Dalton's postulates to explain the laws of conservation of mass and constant proportions.

topics.title: Covalent bonding and naming covalent compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Define a molecule and a chemical bond, and explain why atoms combine to become stable.
Explain single, double and triple covalent bonds through sharing of electron pairs in molecules such as H2, Cl2, O2, HCl and H2O.
Name binary covalent compounds using the prefix system.

topics.title: Ionic bonding and naming ionic compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how atoms form cations and anions by losing or gaining electrons.
Describe the ionic bond and the crystal structure of sodium chloride.
Name ionic compounds and recognise common monoatomic and polyatomic ions.

topics.title: Writing chemical formulae

concepts.learning_objective: Write formulae of covalent and ionic compounds by criss-crossing valencies and reducing to the simplest ratio.
Write formulae containing polyatomic ions, using brackets where needed.

topics.title: Properties of ionic and covalent compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the solubility of ionic and covalent compounds in water, kerosene and petrol.
Explain the electrical conductivity and melting points of ionic and covalent compounds.

topics.title: Molecular mass and formula unit mass

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the molecular mass of a covalent compound from atomic masses.
Calculate the formula unit mass of an ionic compound and explain why ionic compounds have formula units.

topics.title: Production of sound

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that sound is produced by vibrating objects such as strings, membranes and air columns.
Identify how humans, animals and a tuning fork produce sound through vibration.

topics.title: Propagation of sound and the need for a medium

concepts.learning_objective: Explain using the vacuum bell jar experiment that sound cannot travel through vacuum.
State that sound travels through solids, liquids and gases.

topics.title: Sound waves: compressions, rarefactions and longitudinal waves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how a vibrating source produces alternate compressions and rarefactions in a medium.
Distinguish longitudinal and transverse waves and identify sound as a longitudinal mechanical wave.

topics.title: Energy of sound waves and their graphical representation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a sound wave transfers energy, not particles, through a medium.
Interpret crests, troughs and the average density on a density-distance graph of a sound wave.

topics.title: Wavelength, frequency, time period, amplitude, intensity and speed

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate frequency and time period using the relation frequency = 1/T.
Apply v = wavelength x frequency and relate the speed of sound to the medium.
Relate amplitude to energy and explain why intensity decreases with distance.

topics.title: Human perception of sound

concepts.learning_objective: Relate pitch to frequency and loudness to amplitude.
State the human audible range and classify infrasonic and ultrasonic waves.
Distinguish a tone, a musical note, timbre and an octave.

topics.title: Reflection of sound: echo and reverberation

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate distances using echoes and the 0.1 s condition for hearing an echo.
Explain reverberation and how halls are designed to control it.

topics.title: Ultrasonic and infrasonic waves and their applications

concepts.learning_objective: Identify applications of ultrasonic and infrasonic waves in medicine, industry and detection.
Explain echolocation and calculate distances using sonar.

topics.title: Vegetative propagation and its use in agriculture

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that vegetative propagation produces new plants from vegetative parts of a single parent, giving genetically identical plants.
Describe cutting, grafting, layering and tissue culture and explain how they help farmers grow desirable crops on a large scale.

topics.title: Budding, spore formation and mitosis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe budding in yeast and hydra as the growth and separation of an outgrowth from the parent.
Explain how moulds spread by large numbers of light, air-borne spores that germinate in warm, moist conditions.
Explain that mitosis makes asexually produced offspring genetically identical clones of the parent.

topics.title: Meiosis and variation in sexual reproduction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that meiosis halves the chromosome number to form haploid gametes so that the number stays constant across generations.
Explain how the random sorting of chromosome pairs into gametes produces many combinations and variation among offspring.

topics.title: Flowers, pollination and fertilisation in plants

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the sepals, petals, stamen and pistil of a flower and state their roles in reproduction.
Distinguish self- and cross-pollination and relate flower features to wind, water, insect and bird pollination.
Describe the growth of the pollen tube, fertilisation and the development of the ovule into seed and the ovary into fruit.

topics.title: Sexual reproduction and its variations in animals

concepts.learning_objective: Compare external and internal fertilisation in terms of number of eggs and survival of young ones.
Explain the role of yolk, larval feeding stages and post-birth care in the development of young animals.

topics.title: Human reproductive organs and gametes

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the parts of the male reproductive system and state their functions.
Identify the parts of the female reproductive system and state their functions.
Explain gametogenesis and the differences in size, number, nutrients and motility of sperm and egg.

topics.title: Fertilisation, menstrual cycle, pregnancy and reproductive health

concepts.learning_objective: Relate ovulation, fertilisation, implantation and menstruation to the stages of the menstrual cycle.
Describe the stages of pregnancy and explain how the sex chromosome from the father decides the biological sex of a baby.
Distinguish barrier, hormonal, IUD and surgical methods of contraception and explain how STIs can be prevented.

chapters.title: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

topics.title: Biodiversity and India as a biodiversity hotspot

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what biodiversity is and how organisms such as algae, decomposers and pollinators keep ecosystems functioning.
Identify endemic species and explain what makes a region a biodiversity hotspot.
Explain how small differences accumulated over generations gave rise to present-day diversity.

topics.title: Criteria and need for classification

concepts.learning_objective: List the criteria scientists use to classify organisms, from external features to genetic similarity.
Explain how biological classification makes the study of diversity systematic and supports conservation.

topics.title: Classification systems over time and the kingdoms Monera, Protista and Fungi

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the change from Aristotle's grouping to Whittaker's five kingdom system and the reason for each change.
Distinguish Monera and Protista on the basis of cell type, cell wall and nutrition.
Describe the features and ecological role of fungi, including chitin cell walls and saprophytic nutrition.

topics.title: Kingdom Plantae

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the distinguishing features of Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.
Analyse how transport tissues, seeds and flowers reduced plants' dependence on water.

topics.title: Kingdom Animalia

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the key features of the invertebrate phyla from Porifera to Echinodermata.
Explain the role of the notochord and vertebral column in separating chordates from invertebrates.

topics.title: Hierarchy, binomial nomenclature, fossils and threats to biodiversity

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange the levels of classification from kingdom to species and relate shared features to each level.
Apply the rules of binomial nomenclature to write and interpret scientific names.
Explain adaptations and fossils as evidence of change and identify human threats to biodiversity.

chapters.title: Earth as a System: Energy, Matter, and Life

topics.title: The Earth system and its interacting spheres

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the geosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, atmosphere and biosphere with examples.
Explain how a disturbance in one sphere of the Earth leads to changes in the others.

topics.title: Solar radiation, insolation and the solar constant

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the parts of the electromagnetic spectrum in solar radiation and their effects on the Earth.
Define insolation and the solar constant and calculate solar energy received by an area.

topics.title: Albedo, latitude and the role of the atmosphere

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the albedo of a surface to how much it heats up, including the urban heat island effect.
Explain why the spherical shape of the Earth causes uneven heating between the equator and the poles.
Describe the troposphere, stratosphere and ozone layer and how greenhouse gases keep the Earth warm.

topics.title: Winds and ocean currents

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the formation of valley and mountain breezes from uneven heating.
Describe the pressure belts and planetary winds and their deflection by the Earth's rotation.
Explain what drives ocean currents and how they regulate climate.

topics.title: Water and carbon cycles

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the water cycle and how climate change is altering it across the spheres.
Distinguish the fast and slow carbon cycles and the role of oceans and fossil fuels.

topics.title: Nitrogen and oxygen cycles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain nitrogen fixation, nitrification, assimilation, ammonification and denitrification with the organisms involved.
Describe the balance between consumption and production of atmospheric oxygen.

topics.title: Human impact on the Earth's processes

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how fossil fuel burning, fertiliser overuse and deforestation disrupt biogeochemical cycles.
Evaluate local actions and global agreements that help restore the Earth's natural balance.
